## What This Is

This folder contains **architecture guidance** for the Identity and Access Management (IAM) security domain. All content is aligned to TOGAF ADM Phases A–D and the Architecture Content Framework. Documents here define *what* the IAM architecture must achieve and *how* it should be structured — not *how* to configure specific tools or *what* controls to implement.

<!-- AI-GENERATED-START | user:mygainwell | date:2026-10-22 | model:GitHub Copilot -->
> **Enterprise parent:** IAM guidance elaborates the [Enterprise Security Architecture Vision](../GUID-SEC-ARCHITECTURE-VISION-0.0.01.md). The IAM vision is the immediate parent for the capability, ABB, and reference architecture documents in this folder.
<!-- AI-GENERATED-END | user:mygainwell | date:2026-10-22 -->
page_texts.3:
[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/README.md#what-this-is-not]

## What This Is NOT

- **Not security standards or controls**: Configuration baselines, NIST SP 800-53 control implementations, and audit requirements belong in `standards/security/`. Nothing in this folder is enforceable as a security standard.
- **Not Solution Building Blocks**: Vendor product selection, implementation runbooks, and platform-specific configuration are Phase E–F outputs and are not documented here.
- **Not an architecture decision record**: Significant architectural decisions are recorded in `decisions/security/`.

page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/README.md#content-types]

## Content Types

| Type | What It Is | TOGAF Phase |
|---|---|---|
| **Architecture Vision** | Establishes why the IAM architecture exists, its strategic scope, and the success criteria that authorize all ABBs | Phase A |
| **Capability Map** | L1/L2 capability model — the structured, non-ABB description of what the IAM domain does | Phase B |
| **Capability Descriptions** | Narrative elaboration of each L2 capability — what it does, why it matters, who depends on it | Phase A–B |
| **Composite ABB** | The parent Architecture Building Block defining the full IAM architectural hierarchy | Phase B–D |
| **ABB Alignment Matrix** | Traceability catalog mapping every ABB to its L2 capability, status, and paired Reference Architecture | Phase B–D |
| **Component ABBs** | Individual reusable ABBs for each IAM capability area — solution- and vendor-agnostic | Phase B–D |
| **Reference Architectures** | Illustrative, non-prescriptive patterns showing how ABBs compose into deployment-ready architectures | Phase C–D |

## Reading Order

> Start with the Vision. Read capability modeling documents before ABBs. Read ABBs before Reference Architectures.

```text
1. GUID-SEC-IAM-VISION-2.1.01.md          Architecture Vision (Phase A) — start here
2. GUID-SEC-IAM-CAP-MAP-2.1.02.md         Capability Map L1/L2 (Phase B)
3. GUID-SEC-IAM-CAP-DESC-2.1.03.md        Capability Descriptions (Phase A–B)
4. GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md             Composite ABB (Phase B–D)
5. GUID-SEC-IAM-ABB-MATRIX-2.2.07.md      ABB Alignment Matrix (Phase B–D)
6. [Component ABBs below]                  Component ABBs (Phase B–D)
7. ref-arch/[Reference Architectures]      Reference Architectures (Phase C–D)
```
